title: helm(private): values schema + init hooks - tolerations & nodeSelectors + upgrade/rollback handling
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Users running Redwood Private in heterogeneous on-prem clusters need per-component tolerations and nodeSelector support in the Helm chart values schema; additionally we need safer upgrade/rollback behavior for init hooks used during bootstrapping. This PR expands the values schema, threads tolerations/nodeSelector through the templates (init job, controller, scheduler), and stabilizes upgrade hooks with idempotent semantics. Changes include schema additions, template updates, tests, and docs. See the checklist below and the commits for details.
checklist: Add tolerations and nodeSelector to values.schema.json for all components
Wire tolerations/nodeSelector into templates/init-job.yaml and templates/deployment.yaml
Make init hook jobs idempotent and add pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks to avoid resource drift
Add unit tests for values schema and helm template output
Update README values examples and migration notes
commits: add: values.schema.json - include tolerations/nodeSelector for controller, api, initJob
feat(templates): thread tolerations and nodeSelector into init-job and deployments
chore(ci): add helm schema validation test for private chart
fix(helm): make init hook job name stable to allow safe rollbacks
docs: update README values examples and migration guidance
patch_snippets: values.schema.json: added 'tolerations' and 'nodeSelector' keys under each component with proper types and default empty array/object
init-job.yaml: conditionally merge .Values.init.tolerations and .Values.init.nodeSelector into pod spec; added {{ include 'private.fullname' . }}-init stable name
hooks/pre-upgrade-initjob.yaml: added pre-upgrade hook with 'helm.sh/hook-weight' and idempotent check (creates marker ConfigMap)
hooks/post-upgrade-cleanup.yaml: added post-upgrade hook to remove marker on success to allow safe rollbacks
review_comments: Marcus Chen: Can you confirm backward compatibility when tolerations/nodeSelector are omitted? We should default to existing behavior.
Asha Patel: Yes, schema defaults to empty array/object and templates only merge when non-empty, preserving current behavior.
Priya Singh: The init hook name stability is critical to rollback behavior. Please explain why marker ConfigMap is safe in air-gapped installs.

Asha Patel: Marker ConfigMap is created in the same namespace and only carries a timestamp + sha of the applied chart; it avoids re-running long init jobs on transient failures and can be disabled via values.init.useHookMarker=false.
Liam O'Connor: CI failed on helm lint initially due to whitespace in _helpers.tpl; tests look good now. Approving pending green CI.
Priya Singh: Please add a short migration note for operators upgrading from <1.8.0 to call 'helm upgrade --atomic' or disable hooks during manual rolling upgrades.
Asha Patel: Added migration note to README and a short blurb in the release notes section.
testing_notes: Added tests/charts/values-schema-test.yaml to exercise tolerations/nodeSelector combinations
Local k3s smoke runs validated init-job idempotency by simulating a failed init and then a successful retry
Manual rollback test: demonstrated that stable hook name + marker ConfigMap prevents duplicate initialization on re-install
migration_notes: No breaking changes by default - tolerations/nodeSelector are opt-in via values (defaults left empty)
Operators are advised to run 'helm upgrade --atomic' when enabling hooks in production to avoid partial rollouts
To disable hook marker behavior set values.init.useHookMarker=false prior to upgrade if you rely on old init semantics
release_notes: charts/private: add tolerations and nodeSelector support for init job and main deployments
charts/private: idempotent pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks to improve upgrade/rollback stability
docs: migration guidance for upgrades that enable new hooks
